overview: Pelecanimimus (meaning 'pelican mimic') was an early ornithomimosaurian theropod from the Early Cretaceous (Barremian, approximately 126–121 million years ago) of Cuenca Province, Castilla-La Mancha, Spain. The holotype comes from the La Huérguina Formation. At roughly 2.5 metres in length it was a small, lightly built, bipedal dinosaur with an omnivorous or carnivorous diet. Its most extraordinary feature is the possession of over 200 small teeth — far more than in most theropods, and unique among ornithomimosaurs.

Described by Pérez-Moreno and colleagues in 1994, Pelecanimimus polyodon is the earliest and most primitive ornithomimosaur known from Europe and one of the only toothed members of the group. The exceptionally preserved holotype also shows evidence of a soft-tissue throat pouch analogous to that of modern pelicans, and impressions of a possible crest. These soft-tissue details make it one of the most informative Early Cretaceous theropod specimens from Europe.

articles.title: Discovery and Naming
articles.body: Pelecanimimus polyodon was described in 1994 by Pérez-Moreno and colleagues from the Las Hoyas locality of the La Huérguina Formation, Cuenca, Spain. The genus name means 'pelican mimic', referring to the throat pouch evident in the holotype. The species name polyodon means 'many-toothed', alluding to its exceptional dental count of over 200 teeth.

articles.title: Exceptional Tooth Count
articles.body: All other ornithomimosaurs are either toothless or have very reduced dentitions, making Pelecanimimus anomalous with its more than 200 tiny, closely packed teeth. This dense dental array — the highest tooth count of any known theropod — has been interpreted as a filter-feeding or fish-straining adaptation. The teeth are extremely small and fine, suggesting a diet of soft prey items rather than large vertebrates.

articles.title: Soft-Tissue Preservation
articles.body: The holotype preserves traces of soft tissue including what appears to be a keratinous or fleshy beak-like covering over the jaws, a throat pouch similar to that of pelicans, and possible evidence of a small soft-tissue crest. Soft-tissue preservation in Cretaceous theropods is rare and the Las Hoyas locality is one of very few European sites where such detail is preserved.

articles.title: Biogeographic Significance
articles.body: As the earliest known European ornithomimosaur, Pelecanimimus documents the presence of this lineage in Europe during the Early Cretaceous, at a time when Europe was an archipelago of islands. Whether it represents an immigration from Asia or an independent European radiation of early ornithomimosaurs is not yet resolved, but its primitive toothed condition is consistent with an early divergence from the ornithomimosaur stem.

record.description: Pelecanimimus polyodon was a basal ornithomimosaur from the Las Hoyas Konservat-Lagerstatte of Spain, represented by one articulated front half of a skeleton with exceptional soft-tissue preservation.
facts: The specimen preserves skull, neck, forelimbs and anterior trunk but lacks most of the hind body.
It had more than 200 small teeth, unlike later toothless ornithomimids.
Soft tissues around the throat and body outline are preserved, but a pelican-like pouch is not established.
